All rider endpoints validated: POST /api/admin/riders returns NUBO-XXXX code + base64 QR PNG (qr_data_url starts 'data:image/png;base64,'); invalid vehicle => 400; non-admin => 403; GET /api/admin/riders lists with count, non-admin 403; POST /api/rider/activate returns {token, rider} and flips activated=true, invalid code => 404, suspended => 403; GET /api/rider/me with rider token OK and with admin token => 403; PATCH /api/rider/availability?is_available=true => {is_available:true}; POST /api/rider/location => {ok:true}; PATCH /api/admin/riders/{id} suspend/reactivate works and invalid contract_status => 400; POST /api/admin/riders/{id}/regenerate-code emits new code+QR, OLD code => 404 on activation, NEW code => 200. Frontend /rider: rider-activation visible, invalid code stays on activation, valid code → rider-home with rider-name correct, availability switch + start-location button present, token persists in localStorage key 'nubo_rider_token' across reload. Frontend admin: login admin → /dashboard, rider-manager-card visible, full add form (name/phone/vehicle/dni/plate) → rider-qr-dialog shows rider-qr-image (base64 PNG) and rider-qr-code (NUBO-K1O3), count goes 6→7; per-row show-QR, regenerate-code (NUBO-K1O3 → NUBO-RZY3) and suspend (badge → 'Suspendido', toast 'Rider suspendido') all work. REGRESSION: Bloque A pytest tests still pass; founder login still works; AI smart search + admin stats + city manager remain green inside the same module pytest run.

minor.issue: Per-(ip:email) lockout works on localhost (5x 401 then 429) but is INEFFECTIVE through the K8s ingress because the backend reads request.client.host (proxy pod IP, e.g. 10.227.1.2 vs 10.227.1.6) rather than the X-Forwarded-For header. In production an attacker hitting through the ingress will spread attempts across multiple proxy IPs and never trip the counter. Fix: derive client IP from request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host as fallback.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout ineffective in production: routes/auth.py builds identifier='{request.client.host}:{email.lower()}'. Through the K8s ingress, request.client.host is the ingress proxy pod (e.g. 10.227.1.2, 10.227.1.6 — observed in db.login_attempts.find()), not the real client IP. The ingress load-balances even within a single TCP session, so a determined attacker spreads attempts across N proxy pods and never trips the MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=5 threshold on any single (proxy_ip,email) pair. Mitigation (single line): use request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host. Verified on localhost: 5x 401 then 429 (deterministic).
